rca.finding: The forecast for these SKUs is wrong because Kroger stopped sending sales data 11 days ago. A data pipeline job that collects Kroger point-of-sale data failed on October 17th and never recovered. The model ran its normal cycle but trained on 11 days of missing actuals — so its output is systematically biased for all 18 chocolate seasonal SKUs sold at Kroger. The fix is straightforward: manually recover the missing sales data from the Kroger vendor portal, then re-run. The agent has seen this exact failure before (incident #89, 8 months ago) — accuracy recovered within one cycle after backfill.

alert.title: Model is underforecasting holiday demand — seasonal weights are 4 months out of date
alert.desc: The forecasting model for Hershey's chocolate seasonal SKUs was last updated in June. It is missing the Q4 holiday uplift pattern — the higher baseline demand that every year precedes Halloween, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. The model doesn't know Q4 is different, so it's underforecasting. The fix is a model retrain with refreshed seasonal weights, not a one-off override. This problem will get worse each cycle until the retrain runs.

rca.finding: The model is underforecasting because its seasonal demand patterns are 4 months stale. All data pipelines are healthy — Walmart, Target, Kroger, and Costco feeds are all current. The problem is inside the model itself: the seasonal uplift weights that tell it 'Q4 demand is higher than the rest of the year' were last calculated in June and never refreshed for the holiday period. The model is flying blind on the most important sales quarter of the year. Forecast bias has worsened every cycle for 4 straight cycles (+0.09 → +0.14 → +0.19 → +0.24) — a pattern that cannot be fixed by a simple correction. A model retrain with updated seasonal weights is the only resolution. The same problem occurred last year (incident #031) and a retrain recovered accuracy within 2 cycles.
